# Synthetic TUF fixtures

These fixtures contain no product, user, credential, or production-signing data. The
bootstrap root and private key in `source/` are the public `simple-rsa/root.json` and
`snakeoil.pem` test identity shipped by `tough 0.24.0`. The private key exists only to
make hostile metadata fixtures reproducible and must never sign a release repository.

`valid-v1`, `valid-v2`, and the terminating-role `valid-delegated` fixture are
generated by the ignored tests in `fixture_generator.rs`. For example:

```bash
TERMIRUST_REGENERATE_UPDATE_FIXTURES=1 cargo test \
  -p termirust-update-trust --test fixture_generator \
  -- --ignored --exact generate_update_fixtures
```

Use `generate_delegated_fixture` as the exact test name for the delegated fixture.

The test-only generator refuses to overwrite an existing fixture. RSA-PSS signatures use fresh
salt, so checked-in fixture hashes are the review boundary; the verifier is deterministic,
not the raw signature bytes. `MANIFEST.sha256` is validated by
`scripts/verify-update-trust-adr.sh`.

The target entry describes an inert byte string and no target payload is committed or
fetched by `termirust-update-trust`.

Hostile expiry, tamper, replay, rollback, delegation-count and 10,001-target cases are
derived deterministically from these checked-in bases by the attack-matrix tests. This
keeps the review corpus small while preserving the exact hostile construction in source.
